worlds.name: Arrays & Hashing
worlds.tagline: Trade memory for speed: remember what you've seen.
worlds.core_idea: A hash map / set turns 'search the rest of the array' (O(N)) into an O(1) lookup, collapsing nested loops into a single pass.

worlds.name: Two Pointers
worlds.tagline: Two indices moving with a rule beat one index checking everything.
worlds.core_idea: On sorted data (or when you can process from both ends), each comparison lets you safely discard one end, so the search space shrinks every step: O(N) instead of O(N^2).

questions.title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted

worlds.name: Sliding Window
worlds.tagline: Don't recompute the window, update it.
worlds.core_idea: For contiguous subarrays/substrings, add the element entering on the right and remove the one leaving on the left, turning O(N*K) or O(N^2) into O(N).

questions.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock

worlds.name: Stack & Monotonic Stack
worlds.tagline: The most recent unresolved thing is the one that matters.
worlds.core_idea: A stack keeps pending items in LIFO order; a monotonic stack keeps them sorted so each element is pushed and popped once, answering 'next greater/smaller' in O(N).

worlds.name: Binary Search & BS on Answer
worlds.tagline: If you can tell which half is wrong, throw it away.
worlds.core_idea: Any monotonic yes/no condition can be binary searched: on a sorted array, on a rotated array's sorted half, or on the answer range itself ('can we finish with speed k?').

worlds.name: Linked Lists
worlds.tagline: Never lose the next node before you rewire.
worlds.core_idea: Linked list problems are pointer bookkeeping: dummy heads remove edge cases, fast/slow pointers find middles and cycles, and saving `next` before rewiring prevents losing the list.
triggers: O(1) extra space on a list

worlds.name: Trees — BFS & DFS
worlds.tagline: Trust the recursion: solve it for one node, assume children are solved.
worlds.core_idea: DFS answers 'what does each subtree return to its parent?'; BFS answers 'what happens level by level?'. Pick what each call returns and the whole tree follows.

questions.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree

worlds.name: Heaps / Priority Queue
worlds.tagline: Always know the best item right now, cheaply.
worlds.core_idea: A heap gives the min (or max) in O(1) and insert/remove in O(log N). Keep a heap of size K for 'top K', or two heaps for a running median.

questions.title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
Kth Largest Element in an Array

worlds.name: Backtracking & Recursion
worlds.tagline: Choose, explore, un-choose.
worlds.core_idea: Build candidates one decision at a time; recurse; undo the decision. Prune branches that can't succeed. Small N (≤ 20) is the giveaway.

worlds.name: Graphs — BFS, DFS, Topo Sort, Shortest Path
worlds.tagline: Every grid is a graph; every dependency list is a DAG.
worlds.core_idea: Model cells or items as nodes and relations as edges. DFS/BFS for connectivity, multi-source BFS for 'minutes to spread', Kahn's algorithm for ordering, Dijkstra for weighted shortest paths.

worlds.name: Greedy & Intervals
worlds.tagline: Make the locally best choice and prove it never hurts.
worlds.core_idea: Greedy works when an exchange argument shows the local best choice is safe. For intervals, sort by start (to merge) or by end (to keep the most non-overlapping).

worlds.tagline: Recursion + memory: never solve the same subproblem twice.
worlds.core_idea: Define dp[i] (or dp[i][j]) in words, write the recurrence from smaller states, set base cases, choose the fill order. Most interview DP is 'take it or skip it'.

worlds.name: Processes & Threads
